The *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse text preserved within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya, designated as Tha-Ap 372 [SuttaCentral]. As indicated by its title, the poem recounts the past meritorious deed and subsequent spiritual attainment of the elder (*thera*) Saḷalapupphiya, who made an offering of a *saḷala* flower. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records extensive internal Pali text reuse, identifying 64 shared passages across 27 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments 0.3–5.2) and the corresponding female counterpart poem, the *Saḷalapupphikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 12, matching segments 1.1–5.3) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial formulaic verse reuse connects this text to a homonymous apadāna, *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 270, matching segments 3.4–8.1), as well as several other flower-offering apadānas that share recurrent stock stanzas across segments 5.1–8.1, including the *Piyālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 239), *Aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 367), *Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 256), and *Pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 374) [DharmaNexus].
